pk.context: 1 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: It is 80% bound to serum protein, mainly albumin. It is extensively metabolized, primarily by CYP3A4, and excreted mainly in urine.
clues.substance: A white crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 308.8 and no appreciable solubility in water at physiological pH.
clues.product: Under an NDA, tablets come in 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 mg strengths.
clues.safety: The boxed warning covers opioid co-use, abuse, misuse and addiction, and dependence. Contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors except ritonavir; drowsiness (41%) and dry mouth (15%) are most common.
clues.indication: In adults, acute treatment of generalized anxiety disorder, and treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia.
clues.mechanism: It binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors in the brain, enhancing GABA-mediated synaptic inhibition.

tell: Its two active metabolites, 4-hydroxyalprazolam and alpha-hydroxyalprazolam, circulate at under 4% of the parent's levels.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak plasma concentration of alprazolam (C max ) occurs in 1 to 2 hours post dose
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The mean plasma elimination half-life (T 1/2 ) of alprazolam is approximately 11.2 hours
